coverage_note: Large Latin-transliterated stretches 13:41-59:46; many Medi Arabic lines are hidden as [speaking Arabic]/[speaking foreign language] (05:28, 06:13-06:28, 26:46-30:50, 1:02:48-1:09:06) so rows there rest on Amal's echo. 06:28 he asked whether 'ana laazem t9eer' works and Amal said No (a5alliha t9eer) - a question about the rule, left out. ح->ه (بيهمس for بيحمس), dropped ق/ع (dayani, bilax, بنزج) treated as S4 pronunciation; 44:52 vowel-length fix on daaya2ni is pronunciation (F2), left out. Self-fixes left out: 07:34 ستطاش, 07:53 خلت, 37:33 بنوجع, 52:48 dayauna. 27:19 and 28:55 his Arabic is hidden; chat 29:04 gives 'lamma ana biddi ba9eer a7san bi ishi laazem atmarran' but no voiced fix is visible. 1:08:21 thirty rugs singular was his question, right.

rows.chat: EL-YOAM Benet 3ammi badat/ballashat teshte8el fi ma7alli u kaan laazem a3allemha kulshi
rows.why: For 'I had to / should have' in the past he said laazem without kaan; Amal rebuilt it as كان لازم.
rows.english: I had to teach her everything.

rows.chat: EL-YOAM Benet 3ammi badat/ballashat teshte8el fi ma7alli u kaan laazem a3allemha kulshi
rows.why: ta3allamt-ha is 'I learned' (get side, past); to teach her is the doubled-middle a3allemha, bare present after kaan laazem - Amal recast.

rows.chat: EL-YOAM Benet 3ammi badat/ballashat teshte8el fi ma7alli u kaan laazem a3allemha kulshi
rows.why: 3amalt-ha (I did it) is a different verb from teach; Amal replaced it with a3allemha.

rows.chat: el-yoam el-arbi3a, sitta3sh tes3a alfain u sitte u 3eshreen
rows.why: For the month 9 the engine wrote فيسة; Amal echoed 'desse' (likely tes3a). May be an engine mishearing or pronunciation (S4).

rows.amal_said: What excites you؟ One thing. ... No، it's present، بس it's one، not group of things.
rows.why: He used the 'they' form for a singular 'what'; Amal: 'it's one, not group of things' and gave شو بيحمسك.

rows.amal_said: Made. ... Past. He made me excited.
rows.why: 'He made me excited' is past; he used the present bey-; Amal prompted 'Made... Past' and he fixed to hamasni.

rows.amal_said: Get excited, not excite me or someone. ... It's the wrong verb. It's get excited, not excite.
rows.why: For 'get excited' he used the make-someone form 7ammsi; Amal: 'wrong verb, it's get excited' -> t7ammasi.
Command has no present-tense te- prefix on top of the t- form; Amal: 'No T, just one T'.

rows.amal_said: This is why don't you get excited? Why aren't you excited now? ... we are using the adjective here
rows.why: For 'why aren't you excited (now)' he used a negated verb (ma bet7ammasi = why don't you get excited); Amal: use the adjective mit7ammse with mish.

rows.medi_said: Uh, etna hamasna fi el shara.
rows.why: 'We got excited' needs the get-side t7ammasna (chat); he said 7ammasna (we excited someone) and Amal let it pass.
rows.english: We got excited on the road.

rows.medi_said: fi el shara. Or ala el shara? No, fi el shara.
rows.amal_said: street. What's the road? ... Like the way on the road.
rows.why: He used shaare3 (street) for road; Amal: 'street. What's the road?' and he gave ala el taree-. Sheet: 'on the road / way | 3ala el-6aree2 | على الطريق'.

rows.amal_said: الـ safar. Safra is one trip. Safar is...
rows.why: safra is one trip; travelling in general is safar - Amal recast.
'Excite me more' needs the -ni object on the verb; Amal prompted 'Me. Excite me.' and he said hamasini.

rows.medi_said: They got too excited. Humma ziyada.
rows.amal_said: Let's put it at the after.
rows.why: He put ziyada (too much) before the verb; Amal: 'put it after' -> t7ammasu ziaade.
'I was' needs kunt, not the he-form kaan; Amal recast قنت and he fixed to kunnet.

rows.medi_said: Ana kunnet ashtagil bi il AI
rows.why: Working on/in AI: her chat writes fi el-AI; he said bi, she did not voice it.

rows.chat: Ana knet ashte8el fi el-AI, u mit7ammes enno afarjiki
rows.why: 'show you (f)' after the vowel ending -i is -ki (afarjiki); he said afarjinek, Amal recast.

rows.medi_said: In camel. Okay. ... So camel, does that mean like in total
rows.amal_said: We, we need to learn this verb نكمل. Continue. ... ana bakammel ... I continue
rows.why: Didn't-know: Amal introduced نكمل (continue) and explained بكمل vs كامل on his question.
'I hurt you' needs the I-form ba-wajj3ek (her chat); he used the he-form bey- after ana and Amal moved on.
rows.english: Sometimes I hurt you by accident.

rows.amal_said: is did I hurt you? Did you get hurt?
rows.why: 'Did you get hurt?' is the get-side twajja3ti with no object; he put the -ak object on it and Amal said it means 'did I hurt you'.

rows.amal_said: No, by me. ... Because of me.
rows.why: 'hurt by me' on the get-side verb is min + me (minni), not an object ending; Amal said No, by me; he fixed to تواجهتي مني.
rows.english: Did you get hurt by me?

rows.why: 'Don't hurt her' is the doing side twajj3iha, not the get-hurt titwajja3; Amal repeated the prompt and he rebuilt it.
Negative command is ma + the YOU-form (t-wajj3iha); he dropped the t-, Amal 'Very close', he fixed it.
'what you said to me' is 7akaiti + li (la- endings); he said haketni (object -ni, she-form), Amal said ممتاز; her chat has 7akkaitili.
rows.english: I got hurt by what you said to me.

rows.medi_said: daya u-- daya u ni. Daya u ni.
rows.why: 'Did they upset you' needs -ki; he put -ni (me); Amal: 'You.' and he fixed to dayauki.
'What did you get upset about' is the get-side etdaaya2ti (chat); he said dayati (you upset someone) and Amal said Yes. Engine may have dropped the t-.
rows.english: What did you get upset about?

rows.why: Amal voiced عملت right after his amalti; he repeated amalti and she went on, so this may be a cleanup, not a fix. Her chat writes 3meltih (with the -h object).

rows.amal_said: كان بيضايق not ت 'cause it makes people upset. It upsets.
rows.why: 'was upsetting' (makes people upset) is the doing side ydaaye2; he used the get-side itdaaya2; Amal: 'not ت cause it makes people upset'. b- after kaan is not scored (B7).
'they got upset' - he said huwe (he); Amal 'They.' and he fixed to hume.
rows.english: I suppose they got upset with us.

rows.medi_said: Ilbal-- Il, il bilax. Ma, ma ando bilax.
rows.amal_said: ما عنده عكس. ... بس hacks on its own is like the noun for opposite.
rows.why: bil3aks is the expression 'on the contrary'; the noun 'opposite' is 3aks - Amal recast ما عنده عكس and explained. Sheet: 'opposite (bel-3aks = on the contrary) | 3aks | عكس'.

rows.amal_said: La el yameen. ... Bas ana baharrek something la el yameen. From to la.
rows.why: Moving something to the right takes la-, not 3ala (3ala is for giving directions); Amal recast and explained.
rows.english: I moved my bed to the right.

rows.medi_said: so move yourself to the left. Uh, taharki ila shmal.
rows.why: ila is MSA and he dropped el-; her chat writes lalshmaal; Amal only said Mm-hmm.

rows.amal_said: Ashya ak or ashya ek. Ashya e.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he groped for 'your things', Amal supplied ashyaa2ek; he said 'I don't think we've used that before'.

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic] ... Two is ala? ... so is it alawain?
rows.amal_said: هذي الطاولة. And it's لوين. ... We added to the question to always. ... From to is la.
rows.why: His Arabic is hidden by the engine; Amal: 'it's لوين, we added the to to the question' - he asked wain without la-, a preposition that must go in front.
rows.english: Where will you move this table to?

rows.amal_said: ورقة is feminine and one. ورق is plural.
rows.why: His line is hidden; Amal said Nice then pointed out ورقة is one and ورق is plural - he used the singular for 'the papers'.
rows.english: The papers moved from the wind.

rows.chat: lamma 3indna zabaayen u bidna nfarjihom el-sajjad
rows.why: He meant 'when we have' but said 3indhom (they have); Amal said عندنا and, asked what he said, echoed عندهم.

rows.medi_said: nifarijini or nifarj-? It's nifariji, nifariji.
rows.why: 'show them' needs the -hom ending; he said nfarjini / nfariji; Amal recast فرجيهم.
rows.english: we want to show them the rugs
